newsitem.title: INDIA: Pressure grows on India's Gujral to act in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Pressure grows on India's Gujral to act in scandal.

text.p: Political opponents and allies pressed Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Tuesday to force his party leader, indicted in a $280-million corruption scandal, to step down as chief minister of a big eastern state.
But Laloo Prasad Yadav, head of Gujral's Janata Dal party, showed no willingness to quit as Bihar state chief after being indicted on Monday along with 55 others.

"Will the prime minister of India indulge in a widow's wail or act like a prime minister and dismiss the government in Bihar?" Yashwant Sinha, spokesman for the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), told reporters.
"Mr Gujral is on test in this case. His own credibility is on test," Sinha said, calling for the immediate dismissal of Yadav's government in Bihar.
The scandal has rocked Gujral's two-month-old government and stoked tensions within his Janata Dal party.

Last Friday a junior minister in Gujral's government who had been accused in the case resigned. Chandradeo Prasad Varma, who had quit as junior rural areas and employment minister, was among those indicted on Monday.

The Central Bureau of Investigation on Tuesday asked a court in the Bihar capital Patna to issue arrest warrants for Yadav and the other accused, but the court said more documents were needed before it could act.
The case dates back to the 1980s and involves the alleged siphoning off of funds from an animal welfare programme.

CBI officials said on Monday the 56 accused were indicted for cheating, forgery, criminal conspiracy and misuse of official authority. The charges carry a maximum penalty of seven years in jail, they said.
Both Yadav and Varma have said they are innocent.
Yadav's refusal to step down either as Bihar chief minister or as party chief has embarrassed the Janata Dal.
Gujral on Monday reiterated that he believed that Yadav should step down as chief minister, and acknowledged that the scandal was causing trouble for the party.
The four left-wing parties in Gujral's United Front coalition urged the prime minister to seek Yadav's resignation as chief minister

"Failure of the JD (Janata Dal) leadership on this count will not only have negative consequences for itself but will also affect the credibility and prestige of the United Front," the four parties, including the two main communist groups, said in a statement carried by the Press Trust of India.
Gujral, fearing repercussions in his own party, has been reluctant to ask the Bihar governor to dismiss Yadav. But pressure was mounting on him to act.
